column2: During the compression stroke of a metering-pin shock strut, which passage changes size?
column4: Gas charging passage above the piston
column5: Return passage through the recoil valve
column7: As the pin moves through the opening, its changing diameter alters the restriction on the oil. The restriction dissipates landing energy.

column2: Which part of an oil-air strut stores the energy that drives its extension after touchdown?
column4: Oil displaced through the metering orifice
column5: Fluid returning through the recoil valve
column7: The gas charge acts as a spring. The metering and recoil passages control how quickly the strut moves as the gas compresses and expands.

column2: What keeps a wheel aligned as the two cylinders of a conventional scissor-linked strut telescope?
column7: The links allow axial motion while preventing relative rotation of the two strut sections.

column2: Inclined faces inside a nose strut engage at full extension. Which movement should follow?
column3: Wheel turns to face straight ahead
column4: Drag brace folds at its center joint
column5: Piston turns to lock the strut extended
column7: The mating cams rotate the wheel and axle into alignment before retraction. Their engagement depends on strut extension.

column2: Which component limits rapid side-to-side oscillation of a steerable nosewheel during its ground roll?
column7: The damper resists oscillatory motion in the nose gear steering assembly. Steering links transmit the commanded direction.

column2: What information do the spiral colored threads in a coded landing gear bungee identify?
column7: The spiral threads encode a repeating year identifier and the quarter of production. Cord age and physical condition both matter during inspection.

column2: A mechanic finds corrosion on the exposed piston of an oil-air strut. What is the direct concern as it cycles?
column3: Scoring of the seal at the gland
column4: Accelerated wear at the trunnion bearing
column5: Loss of alignment at the torque-link joint
column6: Loss of preload at the wheel bearing
column7: The piston surface passes through the lower seal on compression. Roughness there can lead to leakage.

column2: A retracting wheel brushes its door halfway through travel. Both stops meet rigging limits. What should be checked next?
column7: Check when the door moves relative to the gear. Clearance at the stops does not establish that the wheel clears the moving door throughout the cycle.

column2: What do offset witness marks across a tire sidewall and its wheel rim indicate?
column3: Tire movement relative to the wheel
column4: Axial play in the wheel bearings
column6: Excessive toe angle on that gear
column7: The two portions of the mark originally aligned. Their changed relationship shows that the tire has shifted around the rim.

column2: A tire shows greater tread wear in the center than at either shoulder. Which condition fits that pattern?
column7: Overinflation concentrates contact near the center. Low pressure tends to produce wear toward both outer edges.

column2: With pedal force maintained, how does brake pressure change as anti-skid detects a skid and the wheel recovers?
column7: The anti-skid valve relieves pressure to let the wheel regain speed. As traction returns it restores brake pressure toward the level commanded by the pilot.

column2: On a shock-cord-trimmed ski, what condition most directly determines whether the unloaded runner holds its specified pitch?
column4: Thickness of the runner wear strip
column7: A ski installation can use shock cord to hold the runner in trim. The cord's elasticity and attachment condition affect that attitude.

column2: A single-acting actuator has 2.5 square inches of effective piston area. What ideal force does 800 psi develop?
column7: Multiplying the pressure difference by the effective area gives 800 times 2.5, or 2,000 pounds, before friction.

column2: Which fluid characteristic does a mechanic compare by timing samples through a standard orifice at a specified temperature?
column7: The timed flow through a standard orifice indicates viscosity. The temperature must be specified because it changes the resistance to flow.

column2: A fluid's vapor ignites briefly during a property measurement but does not sustain burning. Which property is being measured?
column7: Flash point concerns momentary ignition of vapor. Fire point requires combustion that continues.

column2: Why does a high-altitude hydraulic installation maintain pressure above the fluid in its reservoir?
column3: To maintain a positive supply at the pump inlet
column4: To establish the actuator's full working pressure
column5: To set the flow rate through the return filter
column6: To determine how far the actuator can travel
column7: Low ambient pressure can limit fluid supply to a pump. Pressurizing the reservoir helps keep the inlet supplied at altitude.

column2: The fluid level falls below the main pump standpipe but remains above the emergency pickup. Which pump still has a usable supply?
column5: Both pumps through their own pickups
column7: The main pickup cannot draw the fluid below its inlet. The lower connection leaves that quantity available for the alternate system.

column2: A brake circuit provides several powered applications after all pumps stop. Which component supplies the pressure?
column7: An accumulator stores fluid under system pressure. Expansion of its gas charge can drive that fluid to the brakes after pump output stops.

column2: A selector swaps the pressure and return connections of a moving double-acting cylinder. With adequate force, what happens?
column4: Its piston continues in the same direction
column5: Its piston locks at the current position
column6: Its piston floats with both ports open
column7: Moving the selector to its opposite working position pressurizes the previously returning side and connects the other side to return. The force then acts in the opposite direction.

column2: Which device opens a path to return when system pressure exceeds its preset maximum?
column7: The relief device bypasses fluid at excessive pressure. A check valve responds to the direction of the pressure difference across it.

column2: A cylinder needs free flow in one direction and metered flow in reverse. Which fitting provides both paths?
column7: The main passage opens in the free direction. A smaller passage remains available when the check seats during reverse flow.

column2: A brake assembly can accept pressure from two independent supplies. What does its shuttle valve do?
column3: Connects one inlet while sealing the other
column4: Blends both pressures at the outlet
column6: Meters the same flow into both inlets
column7: The moving shuttle selects the active source and isolates the alternate line. This lets either supply act on the common outlet.

column2: A pneumatic filter has a bypass around its element. What changes downstream when that bypass opens?
column4: Air still passes through the element at lower flow
column5: Airflow stops at the filter inlet
column6: Air returns through the element in reverse
column7: A bypass preserves a flow path around a restricted element. The normal particle-removal function is lost for the bypassed air.

column2: Why is a chemical dryer fitted after a moisture separator in a pneumatic supply?
column3: To remove residual water from the air
column5: To trap coarse debris before compression
column6: To store compressed air for peak demand
column7: The separator removes much of the moisture carried from the compressor. The dryer reduces the moisture that remains.

column2: An airplane is at 28,000 feet, and the cabin altimeter shows 6,000 feet. What does the lower reading represent?
column4: Pressure at the engine compressor outlet
column7: The cabin instrument expresses the internal air pressure as the equivalent altitude in a standard atmosphere. The differential gauge measures the inside-to-outside pressure difference.

column2: Outside pressure is 4.2 psia and cabin pressure is 11.7 psia. What should the differential gauge show?
column7: Both inputs are absolute pressures. Subtract the outside value from the inside value to obtain the load per unit area across the pressure boundary.

column2: Which valve normally modulates discharge from a pressurized cabin to maintain the selected cabin altitude?
column7: With supply air entering, the controller adjusts the outflow valve to regulate the mass of air retained. The relief functions protect against excessive pressure differences.

column2: Outside pressure briefly exceeds cabin pressure during descent. What action does vacuum relief provide?
column6: Shuts the fresh air supply off
column7: Allowing air inward limits a negative differential across the structure. Positive pressure relief deals with the opposite pressure relationship.

column2: An airplane climbs further after reaching its maximum cabin differential. What happens under normal differential control?
column3: Cabin altitude rises with the climb
column4: Cabin altitude stays at its prior value
column7: The controller limits the difference between the two pressures. As outside pressure falls further, inside pressure must also fall.

column2: What is mixed with cooler air to provide cabin heat in a turbine bleed-air system?
column3: Air from an engine compressor stage
column4: Air from the engine exhaust stream
column5: Air leaving the pack expansion turbine
column6: Air entering the ram-air heat exchanger
column7: Compression raises the air temperature. The system mixes this supply with cooler air before distributing it.

column2: In a combustion cabin heater, what does the overheat protection normally interrupt?
column3: Fuel supply to the combustion chamber
column5: Exhaust flow from the burner tube
column6: Flow through the fresh air inlet
column7: The overheat switch is arranged to stop the heat source by interrupting fuel supply. The temperature control normally cycles the burner to maintain the selected temperature.

column2: A mechanic traces an air-cycle pack downstream from its secondary heat exchanger. Where does the air expand and cool further?
column7: The air gives up energy while driving the expansion turbine. The separator can then remove condensed moisture.

column2: What happens to fine mist as it crosses a coalescing element in an air-conditioning pack?
column5: Ice crystals form on the collector
column7: The element turns fine mist into larger drops. The separator can then direct the droplets into a collector.

column2: In a vapor-cycle cooler, what refrigerant change absorbs heat from the air being sent to the cabin?
column5: Vapor is compressed at the pump
column7: Evaporation requires heat, which the refrigerant takes from the passing air. The condenser later rejects heat to the surroundings.

column2: What varies the refrigerant flow into an evaporator as the cooling load changes?
column7: The expansion valve meters the inlet flow using conditions at the evaporator outlet. This helps prevent starvation or flooding.

column2: A continuous-flow passenger oxygen mask has a reservoir bag. What fills it during exhalation?
column3: A steady stream from the regulator
column5: Ambient air admitted at a vent
column6: Gas released from the relief valve
column7: The supply continues while the passenger breathes out. The collected oxygen supplements the flow available on the next inhalation.

column2: Which sensing element moves the linkage in a mechanical pressure altimeter as ambient pressure changes?
column7: Changes in static pressure deform the sealed aneroid. The mechanical linkage converts that movement to an altitude indication.

column2: How are pressures connected across the sensing diaphragm of a mechanical airspeed indicator?
column3: Total pressure inside, static pressure outside
column4: Static pressure inside, total pressure outside
column5: Total pressure inside, cabin pressure outside
column7: The pitot line supplies the diaphragm. The case around it receives static pressure, so the diaphragm responds to their difference.

column2: In a conventional vertical speed indicator, which air path produces the time lag used to measure a climb?
column3: Static source to case through a restriction
column4: Static source to diaphragm through a restriction
column5: Pitot source to case through a restriction
column6: Pitot source to diaphragm through a restriction
column7: The diaphragm follows the static source directly. Pressure in the case catches up through a restriction, and the temporary difference indicates climb or descent rate.

column2: A digital unit calculates true airspeed using pitot-static inputs and an air temperature probe. Which unit is it?
column7: The air data computer processes sensed pressures and temperature into flight data. It can supply several displays from those measurements.

column2: How does increasing fluid pressure move the pointer in a Bourdon tube gauge?
column5: Its diaphragm expands against a spring
column7: A flattened curved tube changes shape as its internal pressure rises. Linkage carries the free end's motion to the pointer.

column2: The reference junction warms while a thermocouple probe stays at a steady, higher temperature. What happens to the uncompensated signal?
column7: Warming the reference junction reduces the temperature difference between the junctions. Compensation accounts for this effect so the indicated probe temperature stays steady.

column2: A magnetic compass has a fixed line on its housing. What does the card graduation aligned with it indicate?
column3: The aircraft's heading on the card
column4: The magnetic north point of the card
column7: The lubber line is fixed to the case and aligned with the aircraft. The card graduation at that line gives the indicated heading.

column2: A compass card lists paired FOR and STEER headings. Which error does the difference account for?
column7: For each magnetic heading, the card lists the compass heading to steer. The difference accounts for deviation remaining after the compass was adjusted.

column2: A free spinning gyro retains its orientation while its mount is tilted. Which property explains this?
column7: A rapidly spinning rotor resists changes in orientation. Gyroscopic flight instruments use this property to establish a stable reference.

column2: Which energy transfer turns the rotor in a vacuum-driven attitude gyro?
column3: Filtered airflow acts on rotor buckets
column4: An engine-driven shaft turns the rotor
column5: A stator field drives the rotor electrically
column6: Ram pressure acts on rotor vanes
column7: The vacuum pump draws air through the instrument. The flow acts on rotor buckets or scallops to keep it spinning.

column2: A conventional manifold gauge indicates 27 inches of mercury. Which reference defines that reading?
column7: Absolute manifold pressure is measured relative to zero absolute pressure. When the engine is stopped and the manifold has equalized with the atmosphere, the gauge shows ambient pressure.

column2: A transport airplane uses an amber caution annunciation. What response priority does that category convey?
column6: Attention only during the next ground check
column7: A caution calls for prompt awareness with a response less urgent than a warning. The warning category requires an immediate response.
